mcqs.question: Viscosity of a fluid is best defined as:

options.A: The measure of a fluid's resistance to relative motion between its layers.
options.B: The density of the fluid per unit volume.
options.C: The speed at which a fluid flows under gravity.
options.D: The pressure exerted by the fluid on a container wall.

mcqs.answer: The measure of a fluid's resistance to relative motion between its layers.
mcqs.explanation: Viscosity quantifies how strongly a fluid resists shearing motion between adjacent layers. It is not related to density, flow speed, or static pressure, which are separate properties.

mcqs.question: The coefficient of viscosity (η) of a fluid is the constant of proportionality between the viscous force per unit area and which of the following quantities?

options.A: The relative velocity gradient between the fluid layers.
options.B: The absolute velocity of the fluid.
options.C: The pressure difference across the fluid.

mcqs.answer: The relative velocity gradient between the fluid layers.
mcqs.explanation: According to Newton's law of viscosity, F/A = η (du/dy), where du/dy is the velocity gradient. Viscosity does not directly depend on absolute velocity, pressure difference, or temperature (though temperature can affect η, it is not the proportionality factor in the definition).

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes viscous force from other forces acting on a fluid element?

options.A: Viscous force acts parallel to the surface and is proportional to the velocity gradient, whereas normal pressure acts perpendicular to the surface.
options.B: Viscous force is independent of the area of contact, while gravitational force depends on mass.
options.C: Viscous force increases with the square of the speed of the fluid, unlike buoyant force.
options.D: Viscous force acts only in compressible fluids, whereas surface tension acts in all fluids.

mcqs.answer: Viscous force acts parallel to the surface and is proportional to the velocity gradient, whereas normal pressure acts perpendicular to the surface.
mcqs.explanation: Viscous force arises from internal friction and acts tangentially, being proportional to the rate of shear (velocity gradient). Pressure is normal to the surface. Options B, C, and D contain incorrect statements about dependence on area, speed, and fluid compressibility.

mcqs.question: A small steel ball is dropped into a viscous oil and after a short time falls at a constant speed. Which of the following explains why the ball reaches this terminal velocity?

options.A: The upward viscous drag force becomes equal in magnitude to the downward gravitational force.
options.B: The oil’s density becomes equal to the ball’s density.
options.C: The ball’s mass decreases due to dissolution in the oil.
options.D: The temperature of the oil drops, reducing its viscosity.

mcqs.answer: The upward viscous drag force becomes equal in magnitude to the downward gravitational force.
mcqs.explanation: Terminal velocity occurs when the net force on the falling object is zero: weight (mg) is balanced by the sum of buoyant force and viscous drag. In this case, the dominant balance is between weight and viscous drag, giving a constant speed. Options B, C, and D do not describe the force balance that leads to terminal velocity.

mcqs.question: Which of the following changes will most likely increase the viscosity of a liquid at a given temperature?

options.A: Adding a solute that forms strong hydrogen bonds with the liquid molecules.
options.B: Heating the liquid to a higher temperature.
options.C: Reducing the pressure on the liquid.
options.D: Replacing the liquid with a gas of the same chemical composition.

mcqs.answer: Adding a solute that forms strong hydrogen bonds with the liquid molecules.
mcqs.explanation: Strong intermolecular attractions (e.g., hydrogen bonding) hinder the relative motion of layers, raising viscosity. Heating generally lowers viscosity, reducing pressure has little effect on liquids, and gases have much lower viscosity than liquids.

mcqs.question: Two fluids, A (water) and B (honey), are poured down identical narrow tubes under the same pressure difference. Which statement correctly describes their viscosities?

options.A: Fluid B has a higher viscosity than fluid A, so it flows more slowly.
options.B: Both fluids have the same viscosity because the pressure difference is identical.
options.C: Fluid A has a higher viscosity because it is less dense than honey.
options.D: Viscosity cannot be compared without knowing the temperature of each fluid.

mcqs.answer: Fluid B has a higher viscosity than fluid A, so it flows more slowly.
mcqs.explanation: Honey is much more resistant to layer motion than water; therefore its viscosity is higher, leading to a slower flow under the same pressure gradient. Viscosity is an intrinsic property independent of pressure difference, and while temperature affects viscosity, the typical comparison of honey and water assumes the same ambient temperature.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the coefficient of viscosity (η) is correct?

options.A: A fluid with a larger η flows more easily under an applied shear stress.
options.B: The coefficient of viscosity is independent of temperature for all liquids.
options.C: A larger η indicates a greater internal friction, causing the fluid to flow more slowly.
options.D: η is the same for all Newtonian fluids regardless of their molecular composition.

mcqs.answer: A larger η indicates a greater internal friction, causing the fluid to flow more slowly.
mcqs.explanation: Higher η means stronger internal friction, so the fluid resists motion more, contrary to option A. Temperature does affect η (option B is false), and η varies with molecular structure (option D is false). Hence option C correctly describes the relationship.

mcqs.question: Two large parallel plates are separated by a thin layer of oil. Plate 1 is stationary, and Plate 2 moves with speed v. If the distance between the plates is reduced to half while keeping v the same, how does the viscous force exerted on Plate 2 change?

options.A: It doubles because the velocity gradient doubles.
options.B: It halves because the area of contact is reduced.
options.C: It remains unchanged because the speed is the same.
options.D: It becomes four times larger because the viscosity quadruples.

mcqs.answer: It doubles because the velocity gradient doubles.
mcqs.explanation: Viscous force per unit area is η (du/dy). Halving the separation (dy) doubles the velocity gradient (du/dy) while η and v remain constant, so the force doubles. Area is unchanged, and viscosity does not change simply due to geometry, making options B, C, and D incorrect.
